newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest wheat limit down on crop and export hopes.
newsitem.headline: Budapest wheat limit down on crop and export hopes.

text.p: Milling wheat futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) went limit down on Monday due to good crop expectations, an unclear export outlook and Chicago price movements on Friday, traders said.
"The figures that came out today...contributed to the price drop," said Antal Szoke of Agrimpex.
The Agriculture Ministry released on Monday its wheat crop forecast of five million tonnes for the 1996/97 crop year compared with last year's official crop of 3.9 million tonnes.
However, both trade and ministry sources said that last year's crop could have been 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes less than the official figures.
The Agriculture Ministry and Hungary's Central Statistical Office uses crop figures provided by producers which the ministry has repeatedly said are not necessarily accurate.
Milling wheat futures dropped for all maturities by between 380 and the daily allowed 400 forints per tonne, ending at between 21,220 forints for July and 25,210 for May 1998.
With neighbouring countries also expecting good wheat crops this year, Hungary's export outlook was unclear, traders said.

Ukraine said earlier it expected a winter wheat crop of 20 million tonnes, up from last year's 13.1 million tonnes and Romania also expected a record harvest of eight million tonnes, up from last year's 3.1 million tonnes.
Maize prices also finished 200 to 370 forints lower for all but October and November, but turnover remained light due to lack of information to trade on.
Traders said there was no clear trend emerging for maize prices as reliable crop estimates were not yet available.
"The weather is good at the moment for maize but a two-week drought could still have a serious impact," Szoke said.
Total grains futures turnover fell to 692 lots or 305.57 million forints from Friday's 823 lots or 350.43 million forints.
Milling wheat accounted for the bulk of Monday's turnover with 465 lots.
